description: Google's parent company, Alphabet, is an American multinational technology conglomerate holding company. A few of its offerings include an advertising business; its Android phone products; and the Google Chrome web browser, search, Google Maps, and Google Photos. Alphabet also sells apps and in-app purchases through Google Play and YouTube, and offers cybersecurity, databases, and analytics. Its Google Workspace business includes cloud-based communication and collaboration tools for businesses, such as Gmail, Docs, Drive, Calendar, and Meet. Alphabet also invests in other technology ventures, including autonomous-driving company Waymo."

rankings.title: Change the World
rankings.itemDescription: Google, a subsidiary of Alphabet, offers skills programs that support employment, career advancement, and business creation. In early 2026, Google launched an AI Professional Certificate program enabling participants to apply AI to research, content creation, and data analysis. It also teaches participants how to use generative AI to streamline repetitive tasks and create custom tools. In addition, the company enables students and professionals to develop coding skills with its Code With Google initiative, and offers tools like Career Dreamer, which helps users articulate their professional goals.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription: Alphabet became the first Fortune 500 company ever to post $100 billion in annual profit. Ads on YouTube and Google Search were Alphabet’s cash cows, but Google Cloud—which includes its AI efforts—is its fastest-growing division.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription:
Google’s parent company hit important milestones over the past year as it turned its attention to advances in artificial intelligence. Like other tech companies, it saw growth slow in 2022. In January, Alphabet announced it would cut costs by laying off 12,000 employees—the largest layoff in company history.

  • YouTube veteran Neal Mohan succeeded Susan Wojcicki as CEO of the video platform after she stepped down in February 2023. Mohan has pushed improvements to YouTube Shorts to address the platform’s falling ad revenue, which in the first quarter of 2023 registered its third straight quarterly drop.

  • In early 2023, Google set its eyes on rivaling ChatGPT with its own chatbot, known as Google Bard. But Bard’s first live demo produced a botched answer. Alphabet’s market value fell $100 billion that day, though the company’s shares subsequently recovered.

  • Google announced a slate of A.I. products and A.I.-driven improvements in May 2023, including an experimental platform called SGE that would use generative A.I. to power answers in search.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: Google parent Alphabet had a banner year, surpassing $200 billion in revenue for the first time. Alphabet boasted the top-performing Big Tech stock of 2021 as its shares soared by more than 65%, nearly three times the Nasdaq’s 22% gain. It also set aside a whopping $50 billion to buy back shares and announced a 20-for-1 stock split to encourage more investment. Alphabet’s stellar performance was boosted in part by its Google Cloud services, which registered a revenue increase of almost 50%. But while financials were booming, Alphabet faced many challenges on the HR front. Hundreds of workers opted to unionize, after which the company offered enhanced employee benefits including extended parental leave and vacation time; the company’s hybrid-work plans also irked employees who had grown accustomed to working remotely. On the geopolitical front, Alphabet barred Russian media outlets from receiving ad revenue via its online platforms after Russia invaded Ukraine, and transformed its Google offices in Poland into a safe haven for Ukrainian refugees.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: Google’s parent company, Alphabet, faced major challenges in 2020. It was attacked for pushing out two A.I. researchers and got hammered during congressional hearings, and it suffered its first-ever slowdown in advertising revenue. Despite all that, it ended the year with record fourth-quarter sales, after its ad business rebounded from a coronavirus-related lull. Alphabet also benefited from YouTube’s rapid growth, and it invested big money in its cloud business. The company wrapped up 2020 with $182.5 billion in revenue, up 13% year over year, and more than $40 billion in profit. But 2021 hasn’t been easy either. Alphabet still faces federal and state antitrust lawsuits, pressure from a newly formed employee union, and scrutiny over problematic content disseminated on YouTube.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: Alphabet, the parent company of Google, continues to dominate as the world’s leader in digital ad revenue. In 2019, the company generated nearly $162 billion in revenue, an increase of more than 18%, along with more than $34 billion in profit. But Alphabet, along with other big tech companies, remains under regulatory scrutiny for some of its business practices. In Europe, the company appealed rulings that found that it restricted competitor’s ads and broke data privacy laws; France's top court upheld the ruling in June. And in the U.S., regulators are investigating allegations of similar violations. The appointment of Sundar Pichai, the former Google chief, as Alphabet's CEO last December represents a new stage for the Silicon Valley giant; many expect Pichai to impose greater financial discipline—particularly on bold but money-losing "other bets," such as its efforts with self-driving cars and health tech.

rankings.title: Change the World
rankings.itemDescription:
When a company’s name becomes a verb, it’s hard to argue it hasn’t had a big impact. Google, the flagship of the Alphabet holding company, has changed how we find information, navigate the world, and communicate. Underlying most of its products and services is artificial intelligence—it makes Google’s searches better (and thus more valuable to advertisers), Google Translate more accurate, and Google Assistant smarter. The company has made many of the breakthrough A.I. techniques behind these products freely available for others to use.

But Google is also deploying A.I. to directly save lives. Its Flood Forecasting Initiative uses A.I. to generate hyper-local forecasts of rising water levels (as shown here), giving more than 200 million people at risk from potentially lethal floods across India up to 48 hours’ advance warning of dangerous water levels. Since launching in cooperation with India’s government in 2017, the project has issued 27 million alerts. Research Google is conducting with Yale indicates that 65% of those who get an alert take action to protect themselves. Google has extended the system to Bangladesh, where flooding kills some 5,000 people a year. And it hopes to extend it worldwide: Globally, flooding affects up to 250 million people and causes $33 billion in damage annually.

rankings.itemDescription: It’s probably no surprise that a tech powerhouse like Google also caters to its millennial workforce. No. 1 on Fortune’s 2015 Best Companies to Work For, Google is described glowingly by its employees. “While Googlers do love their perks, it’s the innovative technology and the people they work with that stand out for them,” according to Great Place to Work. “Employees are proud to work on projects that change our world like Google Maps and Android.” The perks are, of course, plentiful, too, ranging from themed events, bonuses and employee recognition for a job well done.
